before: Sometimes the urge to get away from what's coming up gets a lot bigger. All of a sudden you need a drink, or that ex doesn't seem so bad after all. Some people start a whole new business. If that's you, it might mean you got close to something that really hurts, and that can be progress, honestly! I'd thank whatever part of you came up with the escape plan, and slow down. If it's more than you can hold right now, I'd get someone steady with you.
after: All kinds of psychoactive drugs can mess with your sense of what's real, and that's often the point of them. But in general, try to select the healthiest ones and use slow and gentle protocols. I'd say one of the most abused psychedelics (aside from ketamine, if you call that a psychedelic) is 5-MeO-DMT. I have a [guide on that](http://bufo.u-dont-exist.com/). People very often believe you need a huge dose of it for a "full release." They go through all kinds of screaming and shaking, nearly killing themselves, with absolutely zero inner-child work being done. It's all spiritual bypassing.

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passages (the passage this carries):
This is also why I caution against forcing your way into intensive meditation, plant medicine, or aggressive trauma processing before enough Nurturer and Protector capacity exists. Those tools can break through protective layers faster than you can build the ability to hold what comes through.

Learn to do inner-child therapy sober, in your ordinary mindstate. When you’re ready, my self-hypnosis guide or lucid-dreaming guide can take it deeper. Low doses of entheogens can also synergize: cactus, CBD tea with sublingual mapacho, Loveyhuasca, iboga, and others.

brief:
- why not blast past with intensive meditation or psychedelics: both can get you past the guards before there's a grown-up big enough to hold what comes through, so hold off until there's enough Nurturer and Protector around; how much is enough depends on the drug
- his San Pedro story and his 21:10 answer: especially at lower doses San Pedro is more protective and nurturing than many other drugs, similar to MDMA, so you don't need as much built up for it; he had some from his good childhood; he still squandered that opportunity; with a better understanding of reparenting it could have been much more therapeutic
- his ayahuasca story and his 21:10 answer: much more challenging at first (huge doses for ego death), not exactly bypassing by itself; reparenting works best with a little connection to divinity; he squandered the opportunity to bring that love down from the heavens to his inner child, which led him to be more like a preacher than a fully well-rounded individual who could lead by example
